activity.title: 🚀 A Week After Cal Hacks 12.0 — Celebrating the Hack with CREAO AI Challenge Winners! It has been a little over a week since Cal Hacks 12.0 wrapped up at the @Palace of Fine Arts. We’re still inspired by the creativity, energy, and brilliance we witnessed from thousands of student innovators. Today, we’re thrilled to celebrate the winners of the Hack with CREAO AI Challenge 🎉 🔥 Best Real-World Productivity ($1,750) ➡️ Tapped In A geo-spatial social productivity platform that uses AI and custom APIs to instantly match users with location-based events. https://lnkd.in/gZmifVKX Team Members: Valerie Eng , Nitya Bhartiya , Laura Guo 🧰 Best Custom Build ($1,250) ➡️ Research Compass An end-to-end AI-powered platform that compresses the multi-week opportunity search into minutes. https://lnkd.in/g5kZ7fFP Team Members: Neelesh Garg , Geng Yudong , Daksh Kumar , Devansh Mishra 🖼️ Best Design Prize ($1,000) ➡️ AI-Powered Food Bank Management System An AI app designed to make the food donation intake process faster and more efficient. https://lnkd.in/gBGvSMYr Team Members: Ethan Lai , William Wang, Eric Wu , Maleeka Raddygala 🔎 Best MCP Integration ($500) ➡️ CivitasX AI-powered system that enabs citizens to interact with civic processes through text, voice, or images. https://lnkd.in/gZhEzdRB Team Members: Kaan Erdem , Rajashekar Vennavelli 🔎 Best MCP Integration ($500) ➡️ AdSensei A platform designed to optimize ad creatives by providing instant and measurable feedback https://lnkd.in/g4Y5s53r Team Members: Samarth Ghulyani , Reet Khanchandani ✨ We’re proud to have been part of this year’s Cal Hacks, meeting so many talented builders and seeing their AI-powered ideas come to life. A big thank-you to the Cal Hacks team for organizing such a smooth and inspiring event — and to everyone who stopped by our booth! ⚙️ Join CREAO and build something epic 👉 https://creao.ai #CalHacks12 #CreaoAI #Hackathon #Innovation #AI #StudentBuilders #Community

BREAKING: OpenAI has released AI agents!! ChatGPT Operator can takes control of your computer, order groceries, book restaurants, and purchase tickets, simultaneously! Check this out: ++++++ CRITICAL NOTE: This is MY EDITED VERSION of their 23 min live demo. OpenAI had *no cuts* in their version. They showed errors, everything - this is just my shortened version. +++++ Okay, first, my favorite parts! 1. AGENTS WORK IN PARALLEL Start ordering groceries, then immediately launch another agent to book dinner reservations. While that's happening, get a third agent searching for concert tickets. Each agent sends you notifications when it needs input. "No table at 7:15 - how about 8pm?" or "This item is out of stock - want this alternative?" 2. YOU ARE IN CONTROL You can also take control anytime - it's like passing a laptop back and forth with a capable assistant. If Operator hits a roadblock, it self-corrects or asks for help. Need to log into a website? It'll pause and let you take over privately. Making a purchase? It always asks for confirmation first. 3. AWESOME PARTNERSHIPS OpenAI partnered with major platforms: OpenTable for restaurants Instacart for groceries StubHub for tickets DoorDash for delivery Uber for rides Target and Etsy for shopping But works with ANY website. No special integration needed. It just sees what we see and clicks what we click. 4. THE ROLLOUT STARTS NOW Live today for US ChatGPT Pro users ($200/month) At operator.chatgpt.com Plans to expand globally Coming to Plus, Team, and Enterprise accounts soon API access in a few weeks 5. SECURITY BUILT IN Requires approval for payments and logins Private mode when you take control One-click data clearing Built-in safeguards against misuse This is just Version One, people. And it is already incredibly powerful.

9 Habits High Performers Swear By These will help you crush it in 2025: Success leaves clues, and they're simpler than you think. High performers don't have superpowers - they've built habits anyone can develop. 9 habits to make 2025 the best year ever: 1. Show up even if you don't feel like it: ↳ Create habits so your actions don't rely on fleeting motivation. ↳ Success depends on consistency. 2. Do it anyway: ↳ Fear, fatigue, and loneliness aren't reasons to stop. ↳ Lean into the discomfort—that's where you grow. 3. Compete with yourself: ↳ Your only competition is who you were yesterday. ↳ Chase growth, not comparison. 4. Face the tough choices head-on: ↳ Avoiding tough decisions creates bigger problems. ↳ Hard decisions today lay the foundations for success. 5. You can't fail unless you give up: ↳ Failure isn't missing the mark; it's giving up. ↳ Every try moves you closer to success. 6. Appreciate your progress: ↳ Celebrate how far you've come. ↳ The journey shapes you more than the goal. 7. Stay humble yet self-assured: ↳ Confidence is steady; ego is shaky. ↳ Trust your skills without seeking applause. 8. Don't let fear stop you: ↳ Fear is temporary; regret lasts forever. ↳ Take action today to avoid tomorrow's what-ifs. 9. Believe in yourself: ↳ Doubt destroys more dreams than failure ever will. ↳ Find the courage to take the next smallest step. True success isn't about luck or perfect timing. It's about showing up daily and building strong habits. Everything you need is already within you. ♻️ Repost to inspire someone. 🔔 Follow Dora Vanourek for more. Visuals credit: @visualhustles

Researchers at Stanford University School of Engineering have developed a lightweight, comfortable knit sleeve that uses pressure-based haptics to simulate touch, opening up new possibilities for wearable devices. The team is working on refining and optimizing their knitting patterns, as well as creating larger-scale devices – perhaps even a full suit – for virtual reality interactions. They also hope to incorporate this work into assistive devices that can help people move or aid in rehabilitation. “Whether the purpose is entertainment, communication, training, or physical assistance,” Prof. Allison Okamura says, “this really brings these wearable devices toward things that people might actually want to use in their everyday lives.” 📸: Andrew Brodhead
